data.title: JPMorgan says Bitcoin price drop widens gap to $86,000 production cost
data.description:
Mining a Bitcoin costs about $86,000, according to JPMorgan. The market currently values it far lower.

The bank's estimate of Bitcoin's production cost now sits more than $26,000 above the market price. That gap could push higher-cost miners to sell more of the coins they've been holding in reserve.

JPMorgan analysts led by Nikolaos Panigirtzoglou published the report on Wednesday. Their central estimate puts Bitcoin's production cost at $86,000.

When the note came out, Bitcoin was trading near $65,000. That left a shortfall of about $21,000 between what the asset fetched and what it costs, on average, to produce.

Two days later, things got worse. On Friday, Bitcoin slipped below $60,000 for the first time since July, stretching the gap past $26,000.

For Bitcoin miners, the electricity bills and hardware costs don't pause when prices fall. The coins they mine are worth less, but the inputs cost the same.

JPMorgan didn't pin the decline on mining economics alone. The analysts pointed to several broader forces weighing on the market.

First, crypto exchange-traded funds saw significant outflows. According to the report, retail investors have been rotating out of crypto ETFs and into stock ETFs.

Second, technology stocks have been deteriorating. Bitcoin has often traded in sympathy with risk assets, so weakness in tech tends to spill over.

Third, expectations around Federal Reserve rate cuts have shifted. When the market prices in fewer or later cuts, speculative assets tend to lose some of their appeal.

JPMorgan suggested that many unprofitable miners may be forced to sell their Bitcoin reserves. Some would sell to cover operating costs. Others might sell to fund a pivot into other businesses, such as artificial intelligence.

JPMorgan's production cost figure has also moved around this year. Earlier estimates in 2026 ranged from $77,000 to $85,000 before landing at the current $86,000.

That upward drift means the bar for profitability has been rising even as the price has been falling. Miners are getting squeezed from both directions.

There's a reason analysts watch production cost so closely. Historically, it has tended to act as a soft floor for Bitcoin's price.

The logic runs like this. When price falls well below cost, the least efficient miners shut off their machines. Fewer machines means less total computing power securing the network, a measure called hashrate.

Bitcoin then adjusts its mining difficulty to match. When fewer miners compete, the puzzle gets easier, and the remaining miners earn coins more cheaply.

The JPMorgan analysts said the gap between price and production cost could narrow if higher-cost operations exit. In that scenario, hashrate and difficulty would adjust downward, lowering the average cost to mine.

Note the word "soft." A soft floor is not a guarantee. Price can trade below production cost for extended periods, and it often does during bear phases.

For traders, the immediate concern is supply. If struggling miners dump reserves to stay afloat or fund AI pivots, that selling lands on a market already dealing with ETF outflows and nervous macro conditions.

For mining companies, the divide between efficient and inefficient operators is about to get sharper. Firms with cheap power and newer hardware can ride out a stretch below the average cost. Those near the top of the cost curve face harder choices: sell coins, cut operations, or change business models entirely.

The macro backdrop still matters, too. JPMorgan tied part of the selloff to tech weakness, ETF rotation, and shifting Fed expectations.

For now, the gap stands at more than $26,000 and the miners are the ones holding the bill.

data.title: TIDEWATER MIDSTREAM AND INFRASTRUCTURE LTD. ANNOUNCES THE FILING OF THE MANAGEMENT INFORMATION CIRCULAR FOR ITS SPECIAL MEETING OF SHAREHOLDERS, IN CONNECTION WITH THE PROPOSED PLAN OF ARRANGEMENT WITH TIDEWATER RENEWABLES LTD.
data.description:
(TSX: TWM)

CALGARY, AB, Nov. 20, 2026 /CNW/ -- Tidewater Midstream and Infrastructure Ltd. () ("TWM", "Midstream" or the "Company") is pleased to announce that it has filed its notice of meeting, management information circular (the "Circular") and related documents (collectively, the "Meeting Materials") with applicable securities regulators in connection with a special meeting of TWM shareholders (the "TWM Shareholders"), to be held on Monday, December 14, 2026 (the "Meeting"). At the Meeting, TWM Shareholders will be asked to consider an ordinary resolution (the "Share Issuance Resolution") to approve the issuance of TWM common shares ("TWM Shares") issuable pursuant to a proposed arrangement (the "Arrangement") under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta), pursuant to which TWM will acquire all of the common shares ("TWR Shares") of Tidewater Renewables Ltd. ("TWR" or "Renewables") not already owned by TWM.

  • The Directors of Tidewater Midstream and Infrastructure Ltd. eligible to vote unanimously recommend that the Company's shareholders vote FOR the Share Issuance Resolution
  • Your vote is important no matter how many shares you own. Vote today!

The Arrangement

Under the terms of the arrangement agreement between TWM and TWR dated November 1, 2026 (the "Arrangement Agreement"), holders of TWR Shares (other than TWM) will receive 0.88 of a TWM Share for each TWR Share (the "Consideration").

Unanimous Board Recommendation and Reasons for the Board's Recommendation

The Arrangement is the result of an extensive and thorough arm's-length negotiation process between the special committee of independent directors (the "TWM Special Committee") of the board of directors of TWM (the "TWM Board") and the special committee of independent directors of the board of directors of TWR and their respective advisors.

The TWM Board, having undertaken a thorough review of, and having carefully considered, among other things, the unanimous recommendation of the TWM Special Committee, information concerning TWR, TWM, the Arrangement and its impact on TWM and affected stakeholders, unanimously recommends (with two directors, one of whom is an officer and both of whom are directors of TWR, abstaining and recusing themselves prior to the vote of the independent directors) that TWM Shareholders vote FOR the Share Issuance Resolution at the Meeting.

In making their determinations and recommendations that TWM Shareholders vote FOR the Share Issuance Resolution, the TWM Special Committee and the TWM Board considered and relied upon a number of factors, including the following:

  • Simplified Corporate Structure: The Arrangement will combine two closely integrated public companies under a unified governance structure to better execute on the combined company's growth strategy
  • Capital Markets Positioning: The increased scale and larger combined market capitalization are expected to improve access to capital markets, with combined company shareholders benefitting from increased public float and trading liquidity. Together with a simplified structure and streamlined messaging, the combined company is expected to be better positioned to attract institutional investors and to have enhanced alternatives for any future financing requirements.
  • Improved Financial Strength and Financing Flexibility: An improved credit profile and capital allocation are expected to build on the optimization potential of each company's existing balance sheet and create additional flexibility to finance future growth opportunities. TWM has received fully underwritten commitments from National Bank of Canada and ATB Financial for secured credit facilities to enhance the financing flexibility of the combined company, refinance existing debt and for general corporate purposes, subject to completion of the Arrangement, which are expected to provide the combined company with enhanced liquidity and refreshed committed tenor.
  • Scale and Diversification: The combined company will have an enhanced strategic position and a more diversified asset base, better positioning it for value-enhancing commercial opportunities across midstream, conventional and renewable fuels.
  • Value Creation Opportunities: The combined company is expected to benefit from operating efficiencies and corporate synergies through public company cost savings, reduced administrative burden and potential tax synergies.

Based on the TWR Shares outstanding as of November 5, 2026, TWM expects to issue approximately 12.8 million TWM Shares to TWR shareholders (other than TWM) under the Arrangement, representing approximately 37% of the outstanding TWM Shares immediately following the Arrangement. Including TWM Shares issuable on the exercise or settlement of TWR equity-based awards and for rounding, the Share Issuance Resolution will authorize the issuance of up to 13,843,838 TWM Shares.

The foregoing is a summary only and is qualified by the more detailed description of the reasons for the recommendation, and of the risks and other factors considered by the TWM Special Committee and the TWM Board, contained in the Circular.

We encourage TWM Shareholders to read the Circular for more detailed information. The Circular is available under TWM's profile on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca and on TWM's website at www.tidewatermidstream.com.

Required Approvals

In order to become effective, the Share Issuance Resolution must be approved by: (a) a simple majority of the votes cast by TWM Shareholders present in person or represented by proxy at the Meeting, including on a disinterested basis, excluding the votes cast by TWM insiders who will receive TWM Shares under the Arrangement, as required by the TSX; and (b) a simple majority of the votes cast by TWM Shareholders present in person or represented by proxy at the Meeting, excluding the votes attached to TWM Shares held by any "interested party", any "related party" of an "interested party" or any "joint actor" of the foregoing as required under Multilateral Instrument 61-101 – Protection of Minority Security Holders in Special Transactions. Completion of the Arrangement is also subject to, among other things, approval by TWR shareholders of the Arrangement, the approval of the Court of King's Bench of Alberta, and other customary closing conditions. Subject to the satisfaction or waiver of such conditions, the Arrangement is expected to be completed on or about December 18, 2026.

Voting and Support Agreements

Directors and executive officers of TWM holding TWM Shares and other key TWM Shareholders, collectively holding approximately 41% of the outstanding TWM Shares have entered into support agreements with TWR (the "TWM Support Agreements"). Pursuant to the TWM Support Agreements, each holder agreed, among other things, to vote or cause to be voted all TWM Shares of which such holder is the registered and/or beneficial owner, or over which it exercises control or direction (including, subject to limited exceptions, any such securities acquired after the date of the applicable TWM Support Agreement), in favour of the Share Issuance Resolution and any other matter that could reasonably be expected to facilitate the Arrangement, and against any matter that could reasonably be expected to delay, prevent or frustrate the successful completion of the Arrangement.

Vote Today

The proxy voting deadline is 9:00 a.m. (Calgary time) on Thursday, December 10, 2026. TWM Shareholders are encouraged to vote well in advance of the proxy voting deadline to ensure their vote is submitted in a timely manner. TWM Shareholders may vote online, by telephone or by any other methods provided in the form of proxy or voting instruction form included in the Meeting Materials.

About Tidewater Midstream and Infrastructure Ltd.

Tidewater Midstream and Infrastructure Ltd. is traded on the TSX under the symbol "TWM". Midstream's business objective is to build a diversified midstream and infrastructure company across the North American gas processing, natural gas liquids ("NGL"), petroleum refining, and renewables markets. Midstream's strategy is to profitably grow and create shareholder value by acquiring and building high quality, strategically located infrastructure. To achieve its business objective, Midstream is focused on providing customers with a full service, vertically integrated value chain through the acquisition and development of energy infrastructure, including downstream facilities, natural gas processing facilities, NGL infrastructure, pipelines, storage, and various renewable initiatives. To complement its infrastructure asset base, Midstream also markets crude oil, refined products, natural gas, NGLs and renewable products and services to customers across North America.

Midstream's downstream assets supply refined products to a niche market and provide an asset base for renewables initiatives. The key downstream assets include the PGR, the sole light oil refinery within the interior British Columbia market, and the Renewable Diesel and Renewable Hydrogen Complex (the "HDRD Complex") owned by Renewables. The PGR refines crude oil feedstock into gasoline and diesel and is where Midstream's co-processing activities take place. The HDRD Complex is also located in Prince George, adjacent to the PGR.

Midstream's key midstream assets include: the Brazeau River Complex, a full-service natural gas and NGL processing facility with natural gas storage pools, and the Ram River Gas Plant, a sour natural gas processing facility with sulfur handling solutions and rail connections.

Additional information relating to Midstream is available on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca and at www.tidewatermidstream.com.

About Tidewater Renewables Ltd.

Tidewater Renewables Ltd. is an energy transition company. Renewables is focused on the production of low carbon fuels, primarily renewable diesel. Renewables was created in response to the growing demand for renewable fuels in North America and to capitalize on its potential to efficiently turn a wide variety of renewable feedstocks (such as canola oil, tallow, used cooking oil, distillers corn oil, soybean oil, and other biomasses) into low carbon fuels. Renewables' objective is to become a leading Canadian renewable fuel producer. Renewables is pursuing this objective through the ownership, development, and operation of clean fuels projects and related infrastructure that utilize existing proven technologies.

Additional information relating to Renewables is available on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca and at www.tidewater-renewables.com.

data.title: US energy firms add rigs; count highest since April 2024 - Baker Hughes
data.description:
US energy firms this week added rigs for a second time in five weeks, energy services firm Baker Hughes said in its closely followed report on Friday.

The total oil and gas rig count, an early indicator of future output, rose by six to 607 in the week to November 20, its highest since April 26, 2024. (BHGUSWTT), (BHGUSOILDRLW), (BHGUSGASDRLW) (USOIRC=ECI), (USGSRC=ECI)

Baker Hughes said this week's increase puts the total rig count up 53 rigs, or 9.6% above this time last year.

Baker Hughes said oil rigs rose by six to 469 this week, their highest since May 2025, while gas rigs rose by one to 128, and other miscellaneous rigs fell by one to 10.

The oil and gas rig count declined by 7% in 2025, 5% in 2024, and 20% in 2023 as lower US oil prices prompted energy firms to focus more on boosting shareholder returns and paying down debt rather than increasing output.

But now with spot US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude prices expected to rise in 2026 for the first time in four years due to supply disruptions from the Iran war, the US Energy Information Administration (EIA) projected that crude output will rise from a record 13.7 million barrels per day (bpd) in 2025 to 13.9 million bpd in 2026, while seeing gas output jumping from a record 107.6 billion cubic feet per day (bcfd) in 2025 to 113.0 bcfd in 2026.

The Middle East conflict has caused the biggest disruption ever to global oil and gas trade and could cut world oil demand by more than 4% by 2035 if governments accelerate electrification, efficiency and fuel-switching measures in response, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said on Thursday.

data.title: Binance hack laundering ramps up as $149 million in bitcoin mixed through coinjoins: Elliptic
data.description:
Launderers allegedly linked to North Korea are now mixing tens of millions of dollars in bitcoin a day in a bid to make tracing the funds harder.

At least 2,310 BTC, worth around $149 million at the time, has been mixed through coinjoin transactions, with roughly 90% of that occurring since Tuesday, Elliptic said in a Friday update.

Coinjoins are a method of obfuscating the source of a bitcoin transaction by combining different users' transactions. This makes it harder to match senders' and recipients' coins.

This follows transfers of around 488,000 ETH, valued at $860 million, from five wallets. Most of this ether is now parked in new addresses, minus around $70 million that was swapped to bitcoin through THORChain. That BTC was subsequently mixed within hours.

The report's author, Tom Robinson, noted the coinjoins were organized by Kruw, a Wasabi Wallet coordinator. Coordinators arrange the transactions to be mixed but don't take custody of users' funds.

The 18,720 BTC stolen directly from Binance are still untouched. The bitcoins being mixed stem from swaps of other stolen assets like ETH, XRP and SOL.

Difficult to cash out

Despite this, Elliptic said very little has likely been cashed out. The firm's latest tally puts about $2.35 billion in wallets linked to the theft, while $2.85 billion is frozen.

Separately, Binance said Wednesday that it obtained a $6.5 billion worldwide freeze order from the Abu Dhabi Global Market Courts against the attackers. Additional court orders give issuers and exchanges the green light to return stolen assets that they've already frozen.

Binance previously described the October breach as a monthslong campaign involving malicious software, a fake job interview and compromised internal AI tooling that gave attackers access to the exchange's wallet-signing systems.

data.title: Boxlight Disclosed Failure to Satisfy a Continued Listing Rule or Standard
data.description:
On November 18, 2026, Nasdaq notified Boxlight that it failed to meet Listing Rule 5550(b)(1), which requires at least $2.5 million in stockholders' equity; its latest reported equity was $1.917 million, and it did not meet either alternative listing standard. Boxlight intends to appeal by the November 25 deadline; a timely hearing request will stay suspension, while trading could be suspended November 30 if it does not appeal. Its proposed compliance plan includes anticipated proceeds from a $2 million financing tranche and an equity line of credit of up to $15 million, subject to conditions.

Original SEC Filing: Boxlight Corp [ BOXL ] - 8-K - Nov. 20, 2026

data.title: Idaho Mule Deer Tests Positive For Deadly Chronic Wasting Disease Near Snake River
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - A mule deer buck hunted near the Snake River has tested positive for chronic wasting disease (CWD), according to Idaho Fish and Game officials.

The deer was hunted in Unit 13, marking the first time the disease has been detected outside five other areas where deer and elk had previously tested positive.

The infected deer was found near an earlier case in Unit 18, about half a mile from the Oregon border.

So far in 2026, Idaho Fish and Game has tested more than 3,500 deer and elk for the disease.

Chronic wasting disease is a contagious and deadly disease that affects the brain and nervous system of deer, elk and moose. There is currently no cure for the disease. It can spread among animals and remain in the environment for many years, making it difficult to eliminate.

'With the hunting season now concluded in Unit 13, we encourage the public to continue supporting CWD surveillance by reporting road-killed deer and elk, animals found dead, and animals exhibiting unusual behavior,' said Stacey Dauwalter, Idaho Department of Fish and Game wildlife health program coordinator. 'These reports and samples are essential to helping us monitor the disease.'

Wildlife officials say their main goal is to keep the number of infected animals low and protect healthy deer and elk populations across Idaho. Since the disease can survive in the environment for decades, completely getting rid of it is not considered possible.

Officials said that hunters can help wildlife experts identify affected areas, understand how common the disease is and monitor changes over different hunting seasons.

data.title: European Markets Close Notably Lower As AI Trade Concerns Trigger Sell-off
data.description:
BRUSSELS/FRANKFURT/PARIS (dpa-AFX) - European stocks fell on Friday and several markets across the region hit multi-week lows - some markets even dropped to multi-month lows - weighed down by losses in several sectors, especially in the technology space amid uncertainty about the sustainability of AI trade despite Anthropic's historic IPO.

After a strong upmove in the regular trading session on Thursday, Anthropic shares fell in after-hours trading and extended its weakness further in today's session, triggering a sell-off in the tech space in European and American markets.

Inflation concerns and fears of monetary tightening by major central banks including the Federal Reserve contributed as well to markets' weakness.

The pan European Stoxx 600 fell 1.68%. The UK's FTSE 100 ended down 0.91%, while Germany's DAX and France's CAC 40 closed lower by 2.13% and 1.6%, respectively. Switzerland's SMI shed 1.02%. The FTSE 100, DAX and CAC 40 shed about 4%, 7% and 5%, respectively in the week.

Among other markets in Europe, Austria, Belgium, Czech Republic, Denmark, Finland, Greece, Iceland, Ireland, Italy, Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Russia, Spain, Sweden and Turkiye closed with sharp to moderate losses.

In the UK market, Polar Capital Technology Trust Holdings ended more than 8% down. Lion Finance, Halma and Ithaca Energy lost 6%-7%.

Babcock International, Scottish Mortgage, Computacenter, Rolls-Royce Holdings, Diploma, Burberry Group, Pershing Square Holdings, St. James's Place, Aberdeen Group, ICG, Smiths Group, Alliance Witan, F&C Investment and IMI closed lower by 3%-5.2%.

Endeavour Mining, Antofagasta, Fresnillo, Rio Tinto and Glencore declined sharply. Bank stocks Standard Chartered, HSBC Holdings, Barclays and Natwest Group also posted sharp losses.

Unilever, Coca-Cola Europacific Partners, Compass Group, British American Tobacco, Rentokil Initial, Admiral Group, Coca-Cola HBC, National Grid, Severn Trent and Haleon gained 1%-2.2%.

In the German market, Infineon tanked 7.6%. Scout24 and Siemens Energy lost about 7% and 6.5%, respectively.

Siemens, Rheinmetall, Hochtief, Adidas, Deutsche Post, Porsche Automobil Holding, MTU Aero Engines, Deutsche Bank, Volkswagen, RWE, Continental, Commerzbank, Siemens Healthineers, Brenntag an BASF lost 2%-4.5%.

Fresenius Medical Care climbed nearly 2.5%. Hannover RE and Deutsche Telekom gained 1.8% and 1.2%, respectively.

In the French market, STMicroElectronics plunged nearly 11%. ArcelorMittal and Legrand ended lower by 5.9% and 4.7%, respectively.

Schneider Electric, Renault, Societe Generale, Dassault Systemes, Kering, Airbus, Hermes International, Stellantis, BNP Paribas, LVMH, Accor, Safran, Saint Gobain, Michelin, Thales and Bureau Veritas also declined sharply.

Capgemini, Sanofi, Danone, Teleperformane, Orange and Edenred posted sharp to moderate gains.

Data released by Destatis showed Germany's producer prices increased at the fastest pace in more than three years in October on rising energy and intermediate goods prices.

Producer prices grew 8.1% year-on-year in October, marking the strongest growth since February 2023. Economists had forecast prices to climb 7.2% after posting an annual growth of 6.7% in September.

On a monthly basis, producer prices gained 1.4% compared to economists' forecast of 0.9%.

The annual increase in producer prices was primarily due to the 18.7% surge in energy prices. The prices of intermediate goods also increased substantially, up by 6.8%.

Data released by INSEE showed France's manufacturing business climate index fell to 104 in November from 105 in October, compared with market expectations of 102, and above its long-term average of 100.

Meanwhile, France's overall business climate indicator fell to 95 in November from a downwardly revised 97 in October, below expectations of 97. The reading was the lowest since June, with sentiment deteriorating across all sectors.

Data from the Office for National Statistics showed UK retail sales rebounded strongly in October, increasing 0.7% in the month following a 0.6% drop a month earlier. Economists had forecast sales to remain flat.

Excluding auto fuel, retail sales grew unexpectedly by 0.9% month-on-month, offsetting the 0.9% decrease logged in September. Sales were expected to drop 0.1%.

On a yearly basis, retail sales growth accelerated to 2.3% in October from 0.4% in September. Excluding auto fuel, retail sales advanced 2.5% after rising 0.4% a month ago.

In the three months to October, retail sales grew 0.4 percent from the previous three months. Food store volumes rose during this period, while fuel retailers mostly recovered from a decline in the three months to July following a spike in March.

Elsewhere, a monthly survey from the market research group GfK showed that British consumer confidence improved in November as shoppers became more willing to make big-ticket purchases ahead of Christmas. The consumer sentiment index rose to -22 in November from -24 in October.

A report from the GfK gorup showed the UK GfK Consumer Confidence Index rose 2 points to -22 in November, recovering slightly from -24 in October, when it recorded its steepest monthly decline since the COVID-19 pandemic.

UK public sector net borrowing increased less than expected in October, the Office for National Statistics said. The government borrowed GBP 17.0 billion in October, which was up by GBP 0.8 billion from the last year. However, this was below the forecast of GBP 18.0 billion.

Central government debt interest payable climbed GBP 2.8 billion to GBP 11.2 billion in October.

data.title: JPMorgan says bitcoin price correction widens gap to estimated $86,000 production cost
data.description:
Bitcoin's recent price drop has widened the gap between its market price and JPMorgan's estimated production cost of $86,000, likely putting more pressure on higher-cost miners to sell bitcoin from their reserves.

Bitcoin was trading near $65,000 when JPMorgan analysts led by Nikolaos Panigirtzoglou published the report on Wednesday, about $21,000 below their central cost estimate. Bitcoin fell below $60,000 on Friday for the first time since July, widening that gap to more than $26,000.

The analysts said miners likely added to the selling as the gap widened. Higher-cost miners may have sold their bitcoin reserves to raise cash, continue operating or fund a move into AI, they said.

"That said, we believe the gap could narrow as the hashrate declines and mining difficulty adjusts as unprofitable miners exit the network," the analysts wrote.

Crypto ETF outflows deepen

The analysts said crypto prices fell sharply over the past two weeks as tech stocks slid further and investors revised their expectations for Fed rates.

Spot bitcoin and ether ETFs, along with leveraged ETFs linked to Michael Saylor's Strategy, saw large outflows in both October and November, similar to May and June, the analysts said. Weekly data showed that the outflows were heavier in the latest two weeks than in the previous four weeks. Equity ETFs, on the other hand, saw inflows.

The analysts said retail investors likely drove most of the crypto ETF outflows because institutional positioning in futures markets largely held up. "Our CME futures positioning proxies suggest that bitcoin positioning has declined modestly, while ethereum positioning remained relatively elevated, holding up even better than bitcoin," the analysts said.

As for retail investors, they may have sold crypto ETFs to fund stock ETF purchases, seeing better opportunities to buy the dip in equities, according to the analysts. They also pointed to a decline in stablecoin market capitalization as a sign that "some capital has also left the crypto market altogether."

data.title: NextEra-Dominion merger cleared by DoJ antitrust division
data.description:
The U.S. Justice ​Department's antitrust division ‌has cleared the $66.8B merger of NextEra Energy and ​Dominion Energy , after noting concerns about the deal's potential impact on electricity costs, the DoJ said Thursday.

The companies' commitment to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission to eliminate their unilateral right to deactivate units in New England "will protect consumers in the region from potentially hundreds of millions of dollars of increased electricity cost," the DoJ said.

In light of the commitment to FERC, the antitrust division decided that its investigation could be closed.

The Virginia State Corporation Commission must also approve the merger, and opening arguments in the state regulator's legal review of the deal began Tuesday.

The proposed merger, announced in May, would create the world's largest regulated electric utility, with a 130 GW large load pipeline, but clean energy groups and Virginia officials have raised concerns about the potential impact of the deal on rates and data center development.

Virginia Governor Spanberger reiterated her earlier demands for a six-year rate freeze, tripling bill credits for families and small businesses, and stronger protections to ensure data centers pay for their energy costs, but the companies rejected the demand for a rate freeze.

The state regulator said this week it will admit into evidence a memorandum alleging NextEra's Florida Power and Light business interfered in Florida elections and politics; the company said in June it agreed to pay $150M to settle investor claims related to the allegations.

data.title: Seegnal Inc. Announces Q3 Filing Exemption and Appointment of a Special Committee to Review Strategic Alternatives
data.description:
CALGARY, AB, Nov. 20, 2026 /CNW/ -- Seegnal Inc. () (FSE: 2I1) ("Seegnal" or the "Company"), a developer of innovative healthcare technology focused on mitigating medication risks, announces the adoption of semi-annual financial reporting. This news release is being filed pursuant to Coordinated Blanket Order 51 – 933 Exemptions to Permit Semi-Annual Reporting for Certain Venture Issuers ("CBO 51-933").

CBO 51-933 allows eligible venture issuers to voluntarily move from a quarterly to a semi-annual financial reporting framework. Seegnal's fiscal year ends on December 31. Under the provisions of CBO 51-933, Seegnal will be exempt from the requirements to file its nine-month interim financial statements and associated management's discussion and analysis ("MD&A") as it meets the eligibility criteria under CBO 51-933, which include being a venture issuer with annual revenues of less than $10 million and maintaining a clean 12-month continuous disclosure record. Accordingly, Seegnal will not be filing its interim financial statements for the nine-month period ending September 30, 2026 and associated MD&A.

Seegnal will continue to file audited annual financial statements (due within 120 days of December 31, 2026) and six-month interim financial reports (due next within 60 days of June 30, 2027). Seegnal remains committed to timely disclosure and will continue to report all material changes and significant developments as required under National Instrument 51-102 – Continuous Disclosure Obligations.

Special Committee

The Company's board of directors (the "Board") has established a special committee of independent directors (the "Special Committee") to lead the Company's evaluation of strategic and financing alternatives.

The Special Committee is exploring a full range of options, which may include, but are not limited to, a merger, sale, related party transaction or other alternative. To assist in its work, the Special Committee may engage professional advisors as it considers appropriate, including legal, financial and accounting advisors.

The Board has not set a timetable for this evaluation process, nor has it made any decisions regarding any potential strategic transaction. There can be no assurance that this process will result in any transaction. The Company does not intend to provide updates or make further comments regarding these matters unless and until it determines that additional disclosure is appropriate or required by law. Seegnal cautions that there are no guarantees that the evaluation processes will result in any particular outcome. The Company will continue to operate its business as usual as it undertakes these evaluation processes.

About Seegnal

Seegnal Inc. () (FSE: 2I1) is an innovative healthcare technology company dedicated to reducing medication-related harm where care begins. The Company's SaaS-based clinical decision support platform is designed to help clinicians prescribe with greater precision by integrating patient-specific data at the point of care, including medications, laboratory results, renal function, allergies, age and other relevant risk factors. By delivering more targeted, context-aware medication insights within existing clinical workflows, Seegnal aims to reduce alert fatigue, support safer prescribing and advance a more personalized standard of patient care. Seegnal's technology is deployed across healthcare settings and is used by approximately 15,000 clinicians in daily practice. For additional Company information, please visit https://www.seegnal.com/ and follow us on LinkedIn.
